headline: On November 21, 2013: Ukraine protests begin over EU deal suspension
captionCards: Yanukovych suspended EU deal after Russia pressured Ukraine
Protests led to the 2014 Revolution of Dignity and regime change
instagramCaption:
Ukraine's streets ignite on November 21, 2013.

Massive protests erupted in Kyiv’s Maidan Nezalezhnosti after President Viktor Yanukovych suspended signing the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement. The move reversed a parliamentary vote favoring closer ties with the European Union. Russia had pressured Ukraine to reject the deal in favor of the Eurasian Economic Union. Protesters demanded Yanukovych’s resignation and condemned government corruption, citing Transparency International’s ranking of him as the world’s top corrupt leader. The violent crackdown on 30 November intensified anger.

It became Europe’s largest democratic movement since 1989 and paved the way for the 2014 Revolution of Dignity.
